candidates.statement: Payment service returns 503 on POST /v1/authorizations, which order propagates as 502 to gateway /v1/orders and /v1/checkout. Traces show payment 503 errors across all three correlation IDs while inventory/redis succeed, so the failing hop is payment, not gateway or inventory.
candidates.uncertainty: No payment-side logs, metrics, or traces are present; the 503 root cause within payment (config, saturation, dependency) is unobserved. Gateway metrics show some /v1/checkout 200s, so impact may be partial.

report.explanation: Gateway 502s on /v1/checkout and /v1/orders trace to order receiving 502 from order's call, which traces to payment returning 503 on /v1/authorizations. Inventory/redis calls succeed. The bounded candidate is an http-500 class failure originating at payment; payment-internal cause requires further evidence.
missing_evidence: Payment service logs/metrics/traces for /v1/authorizations to determine why it returns 503
Payment dependency health (e.g., postgresql) to rule out db-pool-exhaustion or downstream-latency at payment
